messages:
sam.nguyen: Quick sync — Enterprise POC (FinGrid) just dropped a traffic profile + security Q. Need help mapping commit -> reserved GPUs + autoscale policy + pricing impact. They expect ~2k concurrent chat requests sustained, avg 80 tokens/response, and occasional bursts up to ~6k concurrent for ~10 minutes several times/day. They want Dedicated (reserved) + burst capacity. Also asked whether KMS + audit logs in Dedicated suffice for SOC2 or we need Private.

maria.sales: Do we have target p95 latency from them? and their SLA ask?

sam.nguyen: They want p95 < 250ms for short responses (<=128 tokens). SLA ask is 99.9% app-level uptime for inference. Pricing concern: they asked for an estimate of monthly cost at commit + incremental cost for burst credits.

devin-ml: For that workload, rough capacity math: assume 80 tokens * 2k qps -> 160k tokens/s sustained. With batching + KV cache likely effective throughput per A100-80GB GPU (opt config) ~ 35-50k tokens/s for our optimized runtime depending on quantization. So baseline reserved fleet ~4-6 GPUs to hit sustained, but bursts -> need extra warm/idle GPUs or prewarm pool. I'd recommend reserved 6x A100 with 4x burst-capable nodes.

olivia-eng: Autoscale policy notes: we should avoid cold start for 6k spikes. Options: a) reserve extra burst capacity (pre-warmed) b) aggressive prewarm on schedule c) predictive warm based on traffic signals. I'd share an autoscale snippet we commonly propose:
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_instances: 6            # reserved baseline
  prewarm_instances: 4       # warm pool for bursts
  max_instances: 16          # hard cap for burst
  scale_up_policy:           # trigger on concurrency or token-rate
    - metric: concurrent_requests
      threshold: 1200
      step: 2
      cooldown: 30s
  scale_down_policy:
    - metric: cpu_utilization
      threshold: 25%
      cooldown: 120s
```
This keeps p95 low while limiting cost blowouts. We can also enable prefix/KV caching to reduce tokens for repeat context.

darren-ops: One blocker: KMS integration for Dedicated in eu-west-1 currently requires a support ticket and 10 business days to provision customer-managed CMKs. If FinGrid needs customer-managed keys for SOC2, we either push timeline or suggest our dedicated-managed keys + audit logs as interim. Also burst nodes in Private deployments have additional network setup.

maria.sales: Price ask: can finance give a ballpark with 6 reserved + 4 burst prewarm and 2x monthly 10-minute 6k spikes? Include commit discount assumptions (12mo).

evelyn-fin: Ballpark monthly (12mo commit, enterprise tier):
- 6x reserved A100-80GB: $XX,XXX/month (commit rate)
- 4x prewarm burst instances (hot standby): $X,XXX/month
- burst consumption (on-demand tokens during spikes): variable ~ $X-XXk/month depending on duration.
Exact quote pending region + support level. Also note commit terms reduce unit price by ~20-30% vs on-demand. I'll run numbers and post a draft estimate by EOD.

luca-sec: @sam.nguyen re: security Qs — KMS + audit logs in Dedicated generally meet encryption-at-rest & key control sections for SOC2, but checkbox items in their questionnaire we need to answer: key rotation policy, split-knowledge access, access audit retention period, and whether HSM-backed keys are available. If they insist on HSM-backed customer keys or VPC-only control plane, recommend Private (on-prem/VPC). I can prep answers for the questionnaire.

deploy-bot: Deployment window reminder: dedicated-provisioning-eu-west-1 scheduled 2024-04-10T06:00Z for baseline fleet scaling.

sam.nguyen: Helpful — next steps I propose: 1) devin/olivia to firm up recommended reserved+prewarm counts and an autoscale config tuned for p95 <250ms, 2) evelyn to post a draft pricing estimate by EOD, 3) luca to fill the security questionnaire items where Dedicated may fall short and flag any Private-required answers, 4) I'll prep a short deck for FinGrid with capacity justification and cost/risks. Can folks ack?

maria.sales: Ack, I'll coordinate customer expectations and ask them for clarifying traffic curves (minute-level) and SLA flex.

devin-ml: Ack — I'll simulate with current runtime perf numbers and send a 1-page throughput/back-of-envelope by +6h.

olivia-eng: Ack — will include config and a short playbook for prewarm + fallback to a cheaper model variant if tokens surge.

evelyn-fin: Ack — estimate incoming by EOD.

luca-sec: Ack — will draft security answers and flag any items that push them to Private.

sam.nguyen: Thanks everyone — I'll schedule a 30m sync with FinGrid tomorrow and circulate the deck. :thumbsup:
